title: Intraocular Malignancy Mastery: Retinoblastoma vs. Choroidal Melanoma
summary: A comprehensive comparative analysis between the most common primary intraocular malignancies in pediatric and adult populations. This guide synthesizes clinical presentation, molecular drivers, and gold-standard management strategies.

sections.title: Red Flags: Immediate Referral
content: Leukocoria (white pupil) in any child < 5 years old.
Sudden onset strabismus in a child.
Unexplained vision loss + elevated pigmented choroidal mass.
Painful red eye with secondary glaucoma in a phthisical or atrophic eye.

sections.title: Diagnostic Workup Pathway
content: Step 1: Dilated Indirect Fundoscopy & B-Scan Ultrasound.
Step 2: RB: Orbital MRI (check optic nerve). CM: Liver LFTs & PET/CT.
Step 3: RB: Lumbar Puncture (if high risk). CM: Fine Needle Aspiration (FNA) if unsure.
Step 4: Genetic testing for familial counseling (RB1 germline testing).

sections.title: Management Framework
content: Retinoblastoma: Goal is eye preservation and vision. Treatment includes systemic chemoreduction (VEC protocol: Vincristine, Etoposide, Carboplatin), intra-arterial chemotherapy (Melphalan), intravitreal chemotherapy, and focal laser/cryotherapy.

Choroidal Melanoma: COMS (Collaborative Ocular Melanoma Study) criteria. Small tumors: TTT or plaque brachytherapy (I-125). Medium: Plaque brachytherapy. Large: Enucleation vs. Proton Beam Radiotherapy.
Recent Advances: Intravitreal Topotecan for RB vitreous seeds; Tebentafusp for metastatic Uveal Melanoma.

content.explanation: To differentiate suspicious nevi from Melanoma: Thickness >2mm, Fluid (subretinal), Symptoms (photopsia), Orange pigment, Margin near disc, Ultrasonographic Hollowness, Absence of Halo, Absence of Drusen.

sections.title: Clinical Pearls & Landmark Studies
content: RB Landmark Study: Children's Oncology Group (COG) protocols have improved 5-year survival rates to >95%.
CM Landmark Study: COMS study proved that plaque brachytherapy is equivalent to enucleation for medium-sized choroidal melanomas regarding mortality.
Always evaluate the fellow eye in RB; bilateral disease occurs in ~30% of cases.
A pigmented lesion with orange pigment (lipofuscin) is highly suggestive of malignant melanoma.
